I give up. I did not modify `/work/putnam_2025_a5.lean`, so it still contains the original `sorry`.

I checked the statement on small cases and it looks correct. For n=2 the maximum count is 2, attained exactly at the two alternating sequences (+,−) and (−,+). The mathematical content is the known result that alternating up-down sign patterns maximize the number of permutations with that pattern. I don't have a short argument for it, and formalizing it over `Equiv.Perm (Fin (n+1))` for all n is a substantial project. A dynamic-programming or descent-set argument would need many auxiliary lemmas about counting permutations, which is beyond what I can finish reliably here.
